# Comparison of the three requested STAMPED skill candidates

**Recommendation:** preserve the five-skill treatment frozen for the current
study. For a subsequent revision, PR 26 is the strongest source of reusable
assessment machinery and regression fixtures; PR 23 supplies a simpler
inspection-first assessment contract; PR 24 supplies a development and
evaluation plan. None is an already verified replacement for this study's
complete five-skill bundle. PR 26's replay helper needs corrections before
its positive verdict can establish regeneration.

This review combines static inspection on 2026-10-14 with one separate,
coordinator-run no-op negative control of PR 26's replay helper. No skill
was installed, and no frozen skill, harness, task, or reference was changed.
The coordinator completed Workshop local/offline recall and registered-source
freshness checks. The user narrowed this additional pass to PRs 23, 24, and 26;
ASM/Vercel or broader alternative searches were not repeated. This is an agent
recommendation, not a user adoption decision. No candidate workflow was invoked
in the research trials; the separate helper test is identified below.

## Exact source identities

| Source | Pinned head reviewed | What the tree contains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [PR 23](https://github.com/con/skills/pull/23) | [15da761f63a5a45c507e6596a549720bd43a1e84](https://github.com/con/skills/tree/15da761f63a5a45c507e6596a549720bd43a1e84) | `assess-stamped` and `align-stamped`, each with `SKILL.md` and `DESIGN.md`. |
| [PR 24](https://github.com/con/skills/pull/24) | [99e8240fdf49b6184b23dc64e3e911376ea3eb3c](https://github.com/con/skills/tree/99e8240fdf49b6184b23dc64e3e911376ea3eb3c) | Five planning documents under `docs/stamped/`; no STAMPED skill entrypoints in this tree. |
| [PR 26](https://github.com/con/skills/pull/26) | [664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4](https://github.com/con/skills/tree/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4) | Four workflow entrypoints plus `stamped-conventions`, probes, encoder, three creation templates, tests, and saved evaluation artifacts. |
| Current experiment | [8f3acaa4a7c353b6c8ea6928c278478f95328fc5](https://github.com/con/skills/tree/8f3acaa4a7c353b6c8ea6928c278478f95328fc5) | Five requested workflows: align, assess, generic create, ReproNim create, and full research loop, with self-contained supporting references. |

All three PRs were open drafts in the retrieved metadata. The API trees were
not truncated. Downloaded source bytes matched their retained SHA-256 sidecars:
4 files for PR 23, 5 for PR 24, and 97 for PR 26. The
[static inventory](review-inventory.json) records entrypoints, templates, and
manifest presence. The sidecars preserve exact URLs and retrieval timestamps.
These checks establish the inspected bytes, not their correctness at runtime.

## What each candidate contributes

**PR 23 is a compact, implemented instruction pair.** Its
[assessor](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/15da761f63a5a45c507e6596a549720bd43a1e84/assess-stamped/SKILL.md)
profiles the intended object and answers every pinned checklist item with
inspection/execution evidence. Inspection never runs target-supplied code;
guided execution is a separate, explicitly scoped step. Its
[alignment procedure](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/15da761f63a5a45c507e6596a549720bd43a1e84/align-stamped/SKILL.md)
changes the existing agent harness and proposes proportionate options. The
upstream PR states structural validation passed and neither skill had yet been
run on a real project. That is the author's report, not a result reproduced
here. The pair does not contain a creation or research-execution workflow,
bundled probes, or a structured assessment exporter.

**PR 24 is a plan, not installable behavior.** Its
[PLAN](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/99e8240fdf49b6184b23dc64e3e911376ea3eb3c/docs/stamped/PLAN.md)
explicitly says nothing there is implemented. It describes six eventual
skills, including a ReproNim adapter and portfolio self-assessment, and builds
on PR 23 rather than including that implementation. Its strongest contribution
is the [evaluation design](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/99e8240fdf49b6184b23dc64e3e911376ea3eb3c/docs/stamped/evals.md):
concrete task rungs, external scientific grading, fresh-clone replay, controls,
and a budget. Those are useful design inputs, not completed trials or working
creation templates.

**PR 26 contains substantive code and more skills than its body lists.** Its
actual tree has `align-with-stamped-principles`,
`assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles`, `create-stamped-project`,
`do-full-research-loop`, and non-invocable `stamped-conventions`. The four
workflows have operational instructions; they are not empty stubs. Creation
has three real shell templates. The assessor has a probe registry, a response
drafting runner, and a separate replay helper. Conventions contain a vendored
31-item checklist, a tag/commit/hash lock, evidence/status rules, and an encoder.
There is **no `create-repronim-stamped-project` entrypoint** at this head; a
ReproNim planning reference is not that missing adapter.

The body says “two skills” at version 0.2.0, but the actual entrypoints are
0.1.0. The [divergence note](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/docs/stamped/divergence.md)
explains the version reset before first merge. Cite the pinned tree and its
current metadata; keep historical run labels as historical evidence.

## Comparison with the frozen five skills

| Dimension | PR 23 / PR 24 | PR 26 implementation | Current frozen bundle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Assessment | Three-value item answers; Markdown; pinned remote references. PR 24 plans later extensions. | Five statuses, per-item evidence/flags, offline checklist, mechanical probes, JSON and app URL. | Five scoped judgments, rich criterion/evidence schema and checklist side product; scientific validity separate. |
| Independence of one skill directory | Alignment requires the assessor sibling; normative documents are remote. | Workflows require `../stamped-conventions`; alignment also needs creation templates. | Each selected skill bundles its own operating references; sibling reuse has an essential-workflow fallback. |
| Alignment scope | PR 23 edits the harness, then offers options. | Harness changes plus preflight/commit guards and before/after assessments. | Authorized concrete research-object improvements and reassessment, not limited to standing instructions. |
| Creation / ReproNim | Described in PR 24, not implemented in either candidate tree. | Generic creation with templates; no ReproNim adapter entrypoint. | Both generic and ReproNim creation, preserving user tooling and bounded pilots. |
| Full research loop | Planned in PR 24. | Plan, pilot, batch, controls, fresh reviewer, assessment; explicitly disclaims study design/statistical judgment. | Explicit sample/estimand/exclusions/uncertainty/confounder protocol, bounded execution, correctness checks, replay and interpretation. |
| Available evaluation evidence | PR 23 reports structural lint only; PR 24 is a proposed program. | Tests, mutants, saved assessor runs and one R0 run per condition; some results are corrected after harness fixes. | Current study's retained paired worker outputs and separate evaluator evidence; stage 01 assessed with failures preserved. |

PR 26's single conventions package reduces repeated reference material, while
the frozen bundle favors portability of each individually exposed skill. That
is a packaging tradeoff, not evidence that either produces better research.
No `apm.yml`, `apm.yaml`, or `apm.lock` appears in the reviewed candidate trees.
The printed `apm install` example is therefore not a verified installation
contract for this account's metadata-only APM workflow. No temporary-consumer
restore/audit was performed here, and no package-readiness claim is made for
the experimental frozen source either.

The frozen bundle's schema validator also has a real dependency limitation:
stage 01 treatment could not run it because `jsonschema` was unavailable in
the fixed environment. PR 26's standard-library response encoder is a useful
candidate for avoiding that specific installation burden. It validates a
different response contract and cannot simply replace the richer assessment
schema without an explicit crosswalk and tests.

## PR 26 evidence: implemented versus demonstrated

The [evaluation README](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/evals/stamped/README.md)
and [R0 run record](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/evals/stamped/blind-runs/2026-10-13-r0-arms/README.md)
provide more than plans: they retain outcomes, discovered defects, fixes, and
remaining gaps. R0 includes one run each for bare, pointer, implicit-skill, and
explicit-skill conditions. The README discloses that published item counts
were corrected after installed skill copies contaminated the measured object,
and preserves the earlier counts. It also records accidental multi-GB input
retrieval and missing declared DataLad inputs. These are useful failure records.

The PR reports 38 tests, 15/15 scripted mutants, 30/31 item agreement, and
several blind runs. This review read the retained artifacts and code but did
**not** execute those tests or independently reproduce those numbers. Probe
calibration tests mechanical detection; it does not by itself validate every
instruction, scientific result, or replay helper. The saved R0 grading table's
skill-read column is `0/0`; do not use that table alone as proof of skill
exposure. The model, task, host, budgets, and grading differ from this study,
so cross-study timing or score rankings would not be meaningful.

R1 and R2 are explicitly “not started” in the evaluation README. Align/create
entrypoints nevertheless say “exercised at R0–R1”; that broader claim is not
supported by the retained status document. The full-loop entrypoint narrows
its own scope to R0 and intended R1–R2. Treat R1, cluster/GPU execution, and the
missing ReproNim adapter as unverified, not demonstrated features. Alignment
also names `ci-rerun.yml`, but the exact tree contains only
`pre-commit-run-guard`, `preflight.sh`, and `run-recorded.sh` under creation
templates: the advertised CI template is absent.

## Concrete reuse blockers

1. **Replay can accept outputs it did not regenerate.**
   [`fresh_rerun.py` lines 161–188](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles/scripts/fresh_rerun.py#L161-L188)
   copy shipped outputs to a comparison directory but leave the originals in
   the execution clone. An entry command that exits successfully without
   rebuilding them can then reach the identical-digest branch at lines
   195–229 and report `met`. Require removal/quarantine of only declared
   generated outputs before execution, a positive comparison count, and a
   no-op negative control.

   **Confirmed by the separate negative control.** The coordinator ran the
   pinned helper against a local clone of the stopped stage 01 baseline with
   `--entry true` and the already tracked
   `derivatives/gambling-rt/results.json` as its sole declared output. With
   DataLad absent from the bounded PATH, there was no input download. The
   helper reported `status: met` and “All 1 compared output(s) reproduced from
   a fresh clone via `true`.” The command regenerated nothing; the pre-existing
   output survived with the same digest. See the
   [retained result](pr26-noop-result.json) and duct run
   `20261014T224231.526597Z-0dfe2a4de2414d39ad76c9d9d19090bf`.
   This check did not modify the source arm, run a new study trial, or test
   candidate efficacy. It confirms this specific replay-detector defect.

2. **The tolerant table comparison can accept semantic differences.**
   [`_numeric_close`, lines 80–113](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles/scripts/fresh_rerun.py#L80-L113)
   skips cells if either parses as nonnumeric, including changed labels/headers,
   after the whole-file checksum has already differed. A finite/NaN mismatch
   also reaches a comparison with NaN, which does not satisfy the `>` failure
   condition. Require exact schema/label alignment, explicit missing/nonfinite
   policies, and at least one compared numeric cell. The comment “compared by
   checksum instead” does not implement that fallback on this path.

3. **A fresh clone does not prove another host or environment.**
   The helper's [opening claim and implementation](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles/scripts/fresh_rerun.py)
   say it leaves the original machine, but it creates a local temporary clone
   and invokes the entry point locally; a container is optional. It does not
   provision or establish a distinct host. Default `datalad get -r .` also
   fetches broadly rather than a bounded declared input set. Restrict claims
   to the observed environment and add explicit input/resource bounds before
   using it for this project's strict local pilot contract.

4. **Guard installation needs hook composition and attribution integration.**
   The [guard template](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/create-stamped-project/templates/pre-commit-run-guard)
   shows copying directly to `.git/hooks/pre-commit`. Applying that literally
   could replace an existing capture/formatting hook. The
   [fallback recorded-run wrapper](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/create-stamped-project/templates/run-recorded.sh)

The [evaluation README](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/evals/stamped/README.md)
and [R0 run record](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/evals/stamped/blind-runs/2026-10-13-r0-arms/README.md)

explicit-skill conditions. The README discloses that published item counts
were corrected after installed skill copies contaminated the measured object,
and preserves the earlier counts. It also records accidental multi-GB input
retrieval and missing declared DataLad inputs. These are useful failure records.

The PR reports 38 tests, 15/15 scripted mutants, 30/31 item agreement, and
several blind runs. This review read the retained artifacts and code but did
**not** execute those tests or independently reproduce those numbers. Probe
calibration tests mechanical detection; it does not by itself validate every
instruction, scientific result, or replay helper. The saved R0 grading table's
skill-read column is `0/0`; do not use that table alone as proof of skill
exposure. The model, task, host, budgets, and grading differ from this study,
so cross-study timing or score rankings would not be meaningful.

entrypoints nevertheless say “exercised at R0–R1”; that broader claim is not
supported by the retained status document. The full-loop entrypoint narrows
its own scope to R0 and intended R1–R2. Treat R1, cluster/GPU execution, and the
missing ReproNim adapter as unverified, not demonstrated features. Alignment
also names `ci-rerun.yml`, but the exact tree contains only

templates: the advertised CI template is absent.

## Concrete reuse blockers

1. **Replay can accept outputs it did not regenerate.**
   [`fresh_rerun.py` lines 161–188](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles/scripts/fresh_rerun.py#L161-L188)
   copy shipped outputs to a comparison directory but leave the originals in
   the execution clone. An entry command that exits successfully without
   rebuilding them can then reach the identical-digest branch at lines
   195–229 and report `met`. Require removal/quarantine of only declared
   generated outputs before execution, a positive comparison count, and a
   no-op negative control.

   **Confirmed by the separate negative control.** The coordinator ran the
   pinned helper against a local clone of the stopped stage 01 baseline with
   `--entry true` and the already tracked
   `derivatives/gambling-rt/results.json` as its sole declared output. With
   DataLad absent from the bounded PATH, there was no input download. The
   helper reported `status: met` and “All 1 compared output(s) reproduced from
   a fresh clone via `true`.” The command regenerated nothing; the pre-existing
   output survived with the same digest. See the
   [retained result](pr26-noop-result.json) and duct run
   `20261014T224231.526597Z-0dfe2a4de2414d39ad76c9d9d19090bf`.
   This check did not modify the source arm, run a new study trial, or test
   candidate efficacy. It confirms this specific replay-detector defect.

2. **The tolerant table comparison can accept semantic differences.**
   [`_numeric_close`, lines 80–113](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles/scripts/fresh_rerun.py#L80-L113)
   skips cells if either parses as nonnumeric, including changed labels/headers,
   after the whole-file checksum has already differed. A finite/NaN mismatch
   also reaches a comparison with NaN, which does not satisfy the `>` failure
   condition. Require exact schema/label alignment, explicit missing/nonfinite
   policies, and at least one compared numeric cell. The comment “compared by
   checksum instead” does not implement that fallback on this path.

3. **A fresh clone does not prove another host or environment.**
   The helper's [opening claim and implementation](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles/scripts/fresh_rerun.py)
   say it leaves the original machine, but it creates a local temporary clone
   and invokes the entry point locally; a container is optional. It does not
   provision or establish a distinct host. Default `datalad get -r .` also
   fetches broadly rather than a bounded declared input set. Restrict claims
   to the observed environment and add explicit input/resource bounds before
   using it for this project's strict local pilot contract.

4. **Guard installation needs hook composition and attribution integration.**
   The [guard template](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/create-stamped-project/templates/pre-commit-run-guard)
   shows copying directly to `.git/hooks/pre-commit`. Applying that literally
   could replace an existing capture/formatting hook. The
   [fallback recorded-run wrapper](https://github.com/con/skills/blob/664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4/create-stamped-project/templates/run-recorded.sh)
   stages all files and commits itself. In this account it must preserve the
   native Entire, Snapper, and fresh commit-provenance controls and the declared
   output boundary. These are integration requirements, not reasons to bypass
   the current controls or alter frozen workers.

## Proposed follow-up after the current study

Retain all current treatment pins and assessments. Cite the three PRs as
related work and candidate implementation sources, without inserting them into
the running experiment or relabeling its treatment. A next version could adopt
PR 26's pinned offline checklist, per-item provenance/override flags, semantic
mutants, and regression-artifact practice; preserve PR 23's clear distinction
between inspection and executed evidence; and retain the frozen bundle's
scientific protocol, explicit unknowns, and self-contained skill boundaries.

Before adoption, correct and regression-test the replay gaps, reconcile the
missing template and validation-scope claims, compose hooks safely, define the
shared conventions dependency in a supported package, and run a fresh
installation audit. Then conduct a new, separately pinned evaluation with the
same tasks/limits and external scientific checks. Do not use the same probe
implementation as the sole independent ground truth for claims it generates.

# Conventional Commit normalization and DataLad replay

Read-only coordinator audit, 2026-10-14.
The stopped stage-01 treatment's claim is confirmed for its installed DataLad 1.7.1.
This audit did not execute a scientific command, invoke `datalad rerun`, modify the worker, or assess its numerical results.
HEAD, porcelain status, and index entries were unchanged.

The exact transformation commit is `8bac3a2aa1ae82847aca64267704294c106c45f2`.
Its message begins:

```text
feat: record stage 01 RT analysis and verified replay

[DATALAD RUNCMD] feat: record stage 01 RT analysis and verified replay
```

The marker starts at byte 55.
The complete message returned by `git show -s --format=%B` has SHA-256 `b807003b396d5ecd895ed771bd21eac8711d3866fbc2f12cd834e2e0f7ea41df`.

Installed `datalad/local/rerun.py:731-778` defines `get_run_info()`.
At lines 748-752, `re.match()` requires `[DATALAD RUNCMD] ` at the beginning of the entire message.
Its `MULTILINE` flag does not turn `match()` into a search for a marker later in the body.
A pure call to the installed function with the actual commit message returned `(None, None)`.
Passing only the preserved marker-led body recovered exactly the record in `reports/datalad-transformation.json`; the separately retained original `reports/datalad-run-message.txt` recovered the same record.
Attribution trailers appended after the record still parsed successfully.

The commit therefore retains an inspectable transformation record: command, nine declared input paths, two output paths, dataset ID, working directory, exit status, and chain.
Git history and the saved JSON retain useful traceability.
However, `_revrange_as_results()` passes the complete commit message to this parser; the normalized commit is not recognized as a native run record.
A selected range without another recognizable run record reaches the source's `No run commits found` result.
Retention of record bytes must not be scored as successful native DataLad replay integration.

Direct command replay is a separate route.
The preserved transformation is:

```sh
python code/analyze_rt.py && python code/verify_rt.py && python code/build_report.py
```

Its saved report advertises a Pixi-based analysis-and-verification replay command.
These executable entry points do not depend on commit-message recognition.
This audit confirms their recorded presence, not successful execution or scientific correctness; those require the independent replay.

For a future iteration, no native message pattern in this installed version simultaneously starts with a strict Conventional Commit type and the required DataLad marker.
`run(message="feat: ...")` still unconditionally prepends the marker (`core/local/run.py:1144-1156`).
`--sidecar` moves the JSON payload but retains the same marker-led wrapper.
`rerun(message=...)` changes the new message after discovery and cannot fix recognition of the existing commit.
Keeping the marker first and the typed description afterward preserves native parsing, but does not meet the user's strict Conventional Commit subject rule.

A future compatible integration would need an explicit adapter or upstream parser support for a Conventional Commit subject followed by the intact DataLad block.
The current low-level `run_command(..., rerun_info=...)` accepts a parsed record and is what native rerun calls, but still uses the fixed message composer.
Thus it is a possible adapter building block, not an already validated public drop-in solution.
Such an adapter would need tests for record discovery, command execution, subsequent recording, and attribution.

# Stage 01 paired review

Both stopped arms passed the frozen scientific contract and actual direct-command replay from fresh Git checkouts with new locked Pixi environment prefixes.
All five advancement flags in `pair-review.json` are true.
This is an unblinded assessment by the study designer/reference author, who did not author either worker analysis; it has not been human reviewed.

| Observed outcome | Baseline | Treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Worker wall time | 270.242498 s | 358.473083 s |
| Run 01 presented / retained / uniquely excluded | 86 / 85 / 1 | 86 / 85 / 1 |
| Run 03 presented / retained / uniquely excluded | 85 / 85 / 0 | 85 / 85 / 0 |
| Run 01 / 03 median RT | 1272 / 1261 ms | 1272 / 1261 ms |
| Run 03 minus run 01 median RT | −11 ms | −11 ms |
| Reference scalar checks, original and replay separately | 33 passed each | 33 passed each |
| Raw-row, code, flag and retention checks | 171 rows passed each | 171 rows passed each |
| Fresh-checkout scientific outputs | 4 byte-identical files | 4 byte-identical files |
| Provider input tokens (includes cached) | 655,959 | 890,539 |
| Provider cached-input tokens | 599,040 | 825,472 |
| Provider output tokens | 13,710 | 17,808 |
| Provider reasoning-output field | 3,896 | 2,950 |

Run 01 has one absent-response, nonpositive-RT row.
Each independent flag is one, while the excluded-row union is one.
Both reports state the observed valid response estimand, distinguish supplied outside-stage missingness evidence, and avoid population or causal conclusions.
The single participant’s −11 ms difference is descriptive.

Treatment produced an explicit protocol, checklist/assessment artifacts, a skill-use record, and a retained DataLad transformation record.
Its assessment validator and Workshop recorder could not run because `jsonschema` was absent.
The normalized Conventional Commit subject also prevents DataLad 1.7.1 from recognizing its native run record; retained record bytes and successful direct command replay do not establish native `datalad rerun` compatibility.
Baseline used the common provenance controls, supplied verification and replay, and recovered its own Workshop prerequisite failure using an existing environment.
Neither worker was repaired after stopping.

The seven judgments in `assessment.json` are scoped evidence descriptions, with no sum or ranking: Actionability and Modularity are demonstrated; Self-containment, Trackability, Portability, Ephemerality and Distributability are partial.
Identical coarse judgments do not imply identical artifacts or evidence.
New-code license, external-recipient delivery, cross-platform replay and complete offline/cache independence remain unverified.

Replays used the same host and package caches, with public Git/Pixi acquisition.
Scientific outputs were removed before regeneration.
The treatment environment JSON changes only its interpreter prefix.
The report-building layer was not part of the scientific replay.
Parent native capture records the replay commands; there was no new research-agent session in the replay checkout.

Reviewed command paths show no observed cross-arm/oracle read; treatment’s five entrypoint reads appear in native item `item_3`. This is not an OS access audit. Shared home/cache infrastructure and sequential treatment-first order limit the comparison.
One pair and the 88.230585-second difference do not estimate general skill efficacy or model charges.

Reading all five entrypoints and applying selected guidance to a supplied seed does not validate from-empty project creation, a complete ReproNim adaptation, or every full workflow described by those skills.

Machine-readable extraction maps identify exact source files and SHA-256 hashes.
Original/replay comparisons, row audit checks, snapshot identities, input hashes, replay checks and retained failures are under this directory.
`assessment.json` is a study supplement, not a schema-validated upstream assessment record.
# Stage 02 paired review

Both stopped arms pass the frozen cohort scientific contract and actual fresh-checkout replay.
The five advancement flags are true.
The stage03 manifest pins this gate; later assessment and packaging are separate records.

| Outcome | Baseline | Treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wall time | 387.145932 s | 412.516896 s |
| Eligible participants | 16 | 16 |
| Primary presented / retained / uniquely excluded rows | 2736 / 2618 / 118 | 2736 / 2618 / 118 |
| Mean participant median change | 31.34375 ms | 31.34375 ms |
| Participant bootstrap 95% interval | [−70.284375, 132.6578125] ms | [−70.284375, 132.6578125] ms |
| Reference comparisons, original and replay separately | 489 passed each | 489 passed each |
| All emitted trial rows independently audited | 4096 | 4096 |
| Derivative files identical on independent replay | 9 | 6 |
| Final worker Git state | Clean | Three untracked bookkeeping files |
| Provider input tokens, including cached | 1,004,998 | 1,220,003 |
| Provider cached-input tokens | 946,176 | 1,142,784 |
| Provider output tokens | 18,015 | 19,817 |
| Provider reasoning-output field | 5,005 | 4,315 |

Both additionally audit run02, while retaining only runs01/03 in the endpoint. The 118 excluded primary rows have overlapping counts of 117 nonpositive RTs, 118 absent responses and one response-presence disagreement. The positive-RT absent-code anomaly is excluded without repair. Both reports explain the observed-response estimand and sub05/run01 differential missingness.
The mean and interval describe temporal association; neither supports causal practice, learning, fatigue or loss-aversion conclusions.
Both editable figures were independently rendered and reviewed; labels and values agree with the tables.

Treatment adds a protocol, schema-checked project assessment/checklist, explicit skill applications and a worker replay in a fresh offline venv. Its initially missing `jsonschema` prerequisite was recovered using an existing Workshop environment; five feedback records were queued locally. Baseline also recovered the Workshop prerequisite and supplied extensive screening/arithmetic checks, a clean Git state, and a replay wrapper including verification and formatting.
Neither arm produced a DataLad transformation record.
Treatment's untracked analysis stdout, verification stdout and feedback lock were preserved by the coordinator snapshot; scientific code and results were committed and replayed.

Seven-property judgments are in `assessment.json`, separately from science and replay, with no aggregate score.
Scoped Actionability and Modularity are demonstrated; remaining properties are partial.
New-code licensing, external recipient access and cross-platform/offline reconstruction remain unresolved. Post-stop replay reconstructs a new locked environment prefix on the same host with shared caches; this and later native/log packaging are coordinator work, not additional worker-produced quality.

This unblinded design-author assessment has not been human reviewed.
Reviewed command paths show no observed other-arm, earlier-arm or reference-result access; the boundary was logical, not OS enforced.
All five treatment entrypoints were read and selected guidance was applied to supplied seeds.
From-empty project creation, a full ReproNim adaptation, and every complete skill workflow were not tested.
The 25.370964-second difference in this one treatment-first pair is descriptive and does not establish skill efficacy or charges.
# Stage 03 paired review

Both stopped arms produced the correct results for the pinned ds000005 inputs and passed fresh scientific replay.
Treatment does not fully satisfy the reusable screening contract: uppercase or mixed-case missing tokens are misclassified.
The pair gate records that failure separately from actual-data checks.
No worker was repaired, rerun as an agent, or given extra time.

The assessor authored the design and reference and reviewed unblinded.
A second agent, who authored skills, reviewed provenance and schema bookkeeping.
Neither review is an independent human assessment.
Baseline ran first; this is one exploratory pair, not evidence of causal skill efficacy.

## Scientific results

Every variant includes all 16 participants.
Values are equal-participant means of within-person run 03 minus run 01 differences, in milliseconds.
Bootstrap intervals use the frozen 10,000-replicate participant procedure.

| Variant | Mean change (ms) | 95% percentile interval (ms) |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Median, primary | 31.343750 | [-70.284375, 132.6578125] |
| Mean, primary | 58.703828471486 | [-36.589817568534, 150.721339363551] |
| Median, inclusive 0.2–3.0 s | 11.156250 | [-93.71953125, 120.93984375] |
| Mean, inclusive 0.2–3.0 s | 27.709910223933 | [-69.957072765368, 128.120389183602] |

The separate all-three-run context is 1401.625, 1398.40625 and 1432.96875 ms for runs 01, 02 and 03: equal-participant means of individual primary medians, with no additional interval.
Full precision and extraction maps are retained in the normalized JSON.

Both arms pass 2,042 reference scalar checks on each original and replay result.
Independent Decimal audits check all 4,096 trial rows under both retention rules and all 192 variant/run summaries.
Primary retention is 3,942 rows with 154 unique exclusions; band retention is 3,904 with 192 exclusions.
Base flags are 153 nonpositive, 154 absent-response and one presence disagreement; other base flags are zero.
The 191 outside-band flags overlap prior exclusions and remove 38 additional primary-valid rows.

Both reports disclose the sub-15 positive-RT/absent-code anomaly and sub-05/run-01 missingness (65 of 86 offered trials).
Both restrict interpretation to observed valid responses and descriptive temporal association.
All four intervals include zero; no variant is selected because of its outcome, and no causal practice, fatigue, learning, loss-aversion or preference conclusion is warranted.

## Screening implementation defect

Identical pure-function probes cover 15 synthetic cases in each stopped implementation.
Baseline passes.
Treatment fails `N/A` and ` n/A `: its case-sensitive test sets `missing_rt=false` and `invalid_numeric_rt=true`, contrary to the frozen case-insensitive rule.
These two cases yield eight failed flag comparisons across primary/band modes.
Retention remains false.
No such tokens occur in the actual inputs, so the observed numerical results and replay are unaffected.

`screening_contract_passed=false` and the exact checks remain in `treatment-screening-probes.json`, `treatment-evaluation.json` and `assessment.json`.
These probes were added after code review to test an already frozen requirement; they do not revise the protocol.
They do not establish exhaustive correctness for unseen data.
Worker code and its own narrower successful tests remain unchanged.

## Replay, provenance and artifact availability

Coordinator replay used a fresh Git checkout, a new locked Pixi environment prefix and removed derivatives before executing each documented command.
Shared host/caches and allowed source/package acquisition remain explicit limits.
No agent session ran in the replay checkout.

Baseline reproduces seven scientific derivative files byte-for-byte.
Its software record differs only by the expected absolute interpreter prefix.
Treatment reproduces seven regular snapshot files plus one annexed bootstrap table.
Independent checks verify the annex key, original/replay SHA-256 and all 40,000 replicate values against the submitted vectors and seeded resampling procedure.

The original treatment snapshot retains the bootstrap table's annex symlink without its payload.
A separate coordinator attachment at `experiments/03-rt-sensitivity/annex-content/` preserves the verified 1,404,481-byte payload; its manifest records source, key, hash and unchanged snapshot identity.
This attachment does not repair or replace the original snapshot.
Parent-managed storage/publication verification is separate.

Both arms retain actual DataLad transformation records, but their Conventional Commit messages are not recognized by the installed native rerun parser.
Baseline removed the prefix entirely; treatment retains it later in the message.
Direct scientific replay succeeds.
This gap is retained in the two provenance reviews, not counted as successful native DataLad integration.

## Research-object qualities and effort

The seven properties are judged separately, without an aggregate score.
Both demonstrate bounded Actionability and Modularity.
Self-containment, Trackability, Portability, Ephemerality and Distributability remain partial because dependency closure, native replay integration, independent-host execution, complete environment disposal and new-code licensing/recipient retrieval are unresolved.

Treatment adds a pre-analysis protocol, five scoped skill-use records, schema-validated assessment bookkeeping, all 31 checklist responses, a retained bootstrap table and a disposable-directory/venv worker check.
Baseline renders its figure, records its host formatting dependency, checks manifest hashes and retains focused tests and arithmetic verification.
Treatment explicitly checked SVG structure without rendering; coordinator rendering verifies both figures but does not improve worker-produced quality.

Both commits are clean.
Baseline used 382.979 seconds; treatment used 474.465 seconds, within their equal 480-second caps.
Provider input/output totals and separate replay phase timings are retained in `assessment.json`; token totals include cached input and are not monetary cost estimates.
Baseline's initial denominator assertion and ancillary dependency failure were recovered within the attempt.

+# STAMPED skills: pinned exploratory study
+
+The experimental bundle is [commit `8f3acaa4a7c353b6c8ea6928c278478f95328fc5`](https://github.com/con/skills/tree/8f3acaa4a7c353b6c8ea6928c278478f95328fc5), with all five skills at `0.1.0`.
+This documentation delivery preserves those five trees exactly.
+The four core workflows remain tool-neutral; domain and tool preferences remain in the ReproNim creation adapter.
+See the [skill index](../../README.md#stamped-research-skills-experimental) for their distinct scopes.
+
+## Study and source identities
+
+Three sequential baseline/treatment pairs tested additional procedural guidance in preconfigured research projects, with common scientific tasks, locked tools, offline STAMPED references, account controls, `gpt-6-astra`/`ultra`, and 480-second worker caps.
+Treatment read the five pinned entrypoints and applied selected steps; baseline already had substantial research and provenance guidance.
+Treatment ran first in stages 01/02; baseline ran first in stage 03.
+A bounded amendment for changed shared model defaults preserved the explicit worker model/effort overrides; it did not establish constant account history.
+The coordinator confirmed all six workers stopped before this documentation continuation; none received post-stop repairs.
+
+The replacement study used [OpenNeuro ds000005 at `b094fc2f41487f92d382a1a432165ae58caae386`](https://github.com/OpenNeuroDatasets/ds000005/tree/b094fc2f41487f92d382a1a432165ae58caae386): 48 event files, 16 participants, and 4,096 rows.
+It describes recorded response times across runs, not MRI processing or the original loss-aversion model.
+The originally proposed ABCD reproduction was not performed because access was unavailable; an ambiguous Flanker candidate was rejected before experimental launch.
+
+The design pass consulted these immutable sources:
+
+| Source | Revision / role |
+| --- | --- |
+| [STAMPED paper](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-paper/tree/310eefa1bd756a04d69161c216d93af4d354dd05) | `310eefa1bd756a04d69161c216d93af4d354dd05`; detailed normative principles. |
+| [Principles schema](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-principles-schema/tree/929e87db4e1248aa6b3b32c368da9e825137175e) | `929e87db4e1248aa6b3b32c368da9e825137175e`; principles data 0.2.0. |
+| [Checklist schema](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-checklist-schema/tree/8826b99e15f1db1cc2f0d691d892786a4bb51815) | `8826b99e15f1db1cc2f0d691d892786a4bb51815`; checklist 0.3.1. |
+| [Checklist UI](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-checklist/tree/d24d7ca0515efa6ed639ef2844c351c8e5471154) | `d24d7ca0515efa6ed639ef2844c351c8e5471154`; response format 3. |
+| [Agent-skill discussion](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-agent-skills/tree/a723c24585799e121c3f5ba046b1f50901492719) | `a723c24585799e121c3f5ba046b1f50901492719`; scope and decomposition. |
+| [Assessment model](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-skills-assessment/tree/c4c0428e6962a631d910d0becb00b7bb1c3c903c) | `c4c0428e6962a631d910d0becb00b7bb1c3c903c`; evidence/review distinctions. |
+| [Examples](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-examples/tree/5944d90004fbaa5e992d2764728cfd6992b8b12f) | `5944d90004fbaa5e992d2764728cfd6992b8b12f`; illustrative, with curation states preserved. |
+
+The [module manifest](logs/manifest.json) records the checked report, design notes, three final assessments/reviews, candidate review, DataLad audit, and export-plan identities.
+Its five treatment-tree SHA-256 values match both stage-01 and stage-03 manifests and the historical Git trees.
+The earlier draft artifact manifest predates Snapper formatting and is not the experimental tree pin.
+Paper/schema identifier and licensing-requirement differences remain source-qualified.
+
+The [full report][report], [design notes][design], and [final stage assessments][evaluations] are coordinator publication targets on the study review branch; their checked local bytes are identified in the manifest, and final upload/retrieval verification remains coordinator work.
+The design notes' statement that evaluation was pending describes the earlier implementation pass; the completed report and final assessments govern this summary.
+
+## What was checked
+
+| Pair | Numerical checks on each original and replay | Direct scientific command replay |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| [01: one participant][stage01] | 33 scalar comparisons and 171 rows; median change −11 ms. | Four scientific files byte-identical in each arm. |
+| [02: cohort][stage02] | 489 scalar comparisons and 4,096 audited rows; mean within-person median change +31.34375 ms, 95% bootstrap interval [−70.284375, 132.6578125] ms. | Nine baseline and six treatment derivative files byte-identical. |
+| [03: sensitivity][stage03] | 2,042 scalar comparisons, 4,096 rows under two rules, and 192 variant/run summaries; all four intervals include zero. | Seven regular files per arm plus treatment's separately verified annexed bootstrap table; all 40,000 replicate values checked. |
+
+These are descriptive response-time results, with differential missingness and run/task composition limiting interpretation.
+They do not establish causal practice, fatigue, learning, or loss-aversion effects.
+
+**Stage 03 treatment failed an independent screening-contract check.**
+Identical 15-case probes found `N/A` and ` n/A ` labeled `invalid_numeric_rt` instead of `missing_rt`, contrary to the frozen case-insensitive requirement; baseline passed the probes.
+The two cases caused eight failed flag comparisons across the primary/band modes.
+Those variants are absent from the pinned data, so numerical endpoints and command replay still passed.
+The worker defect remains unrepaired; complete output-contract success is not claimed.
+
+Fresh coordinator replay removed scientific outputs, used new checkouts and locked environment prefixes, and regenerated results on the same host with shared caches and permitted public acquisition.
+This does not demonstrate offline dependency closure, another platform, or complete report-builder replay.
+The stage-03 annex payload was separately attached by the coordinator; the original snapshot's targetless annex link was preserved.
+
+**Native DataLad rerun is a separate, unresolved integration result.**
+Stage-01 treatment and both stage-03 arms retained transformation records, but installed DataLad 1.7.1 requires `[DATALAD RUNCMD]` at the very beginning of the commit message.
+Mandatory Conventional Commit subjects prevent native discovery; placing the marker later in the message does not satisfy that parser.
+Direct command replay passed, but retained record bytes do not demonstrate successful native `datalad rerun`.
+Neither stage-02 arm recorded a DataLad transformation.
+The [read-only parser audit][datalad] preserves the incompatibility without patching workers or granting a commit-policy exception.
+
+**Research-object judgments remain separate from numerical and replay checks.**
+All six assessments judged scoped Actionability and Modularity demonstrated, and Self-containment, Trackability, Portability, Ephemerality, and Distributability partial.
+There is no aggregate score; matching coarse judgments conceal different evidence and gaps.
+Treatment added explicit protocol/assessment records and took longer in each pair; this is not a causal cost or efficacy estimate.
+Assessment was unblinded by the study designer/reference implementer, without independent human review; shared-account logical isolation and one pair per stage further limit inference.
+Reading five entrypoints in supplied seeds does not validate from-empty creation, every complete skill workflow, a full ReproNim adaptation, HPC, or an imaging pipeline.
+
+## Validation and reuse limits
+
+The design pass's focused checks covered local links, metadata, Python syntax, schema invariants, checklist coverage/version refusal, five-state mapping, UTF-16 limits, and URL round trips on synthetic fixtures.
+The repository validator checked the five skills with zero errors and five optional `allowed-tools` warnings.
+The stock skill-creator validator rejects the top-level `version` required here; canonical files retain `version: 0.1.0`.
+These are structural/helper checks, not proof of scientific truth or every workflow.
+
+The optional formal-validation route requires `jsonschema>=4,<5`.
+Stage-01 treatment could not execute its assessment validator or Workshop recorder because that prerequisite was missing; the failures remain failed.
+Later stages recovered using an already installed Workshop environment, without repairing stage 01.
+Passing the experimental schema/bookkeeping contract does not establish upstream assessment-package compatibility.
+Stage-02 treatment also left two stdout files and a feedback lock untracked; the stopped snapshot retained them.
+
+This experiment exposed source directories directly; it did not validate APM packaging, installation, frozen restoration, or audit.
+No complete APM installation contract is claimed.
+The dataset declares PDDL v1.0 and attribution to Tom et al. (2007); those terms do not license new code or these skills.
+Repository licensing remains TBD, and unresolved upstream/new-code permissions and independent-recipient delivery remain unresolved.
+
+## Related candidate reviews
+
+The [pinned candidate review][candidates] considered these alternatives without adopting their implementations or changing the treatment:
+
+| Candidate | Reviewed head | Scope |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| [PR 23](https://github.com/con/skills/pull/23) | `15da761f63a5a45c507e6596a549720bd43a1e84` | Assessment/alignment instruction pair; reported structural checks, no reported real-project execution. |
+| [PR 24](https://github.com/con/skills/pull/24) | `99e8240fdf49b6184b23dc64e3e911376ea3eb3c` | Planning/evaluation documents; no implemented STAMPED entrypoints. |
+| [PR 26](https://github.com/con/skills/pull/26) | `664d48bafca7e05d942707713bd896f95932b3a4` | Four workflow skills plus conventions, probes, templates, tests, and saved evaluations; no ReproNim creation entrypoint. |
+
+Candidate-reported test/agreement numbers were not independently reproduced.
+A separate coordinator no-op control confirmed that PR 26's pinned replay detector could accept an unchanged pre-existing output after running `true`.
+That specific defect check was not a study arm or a general candidate-efficacy verdict.
+None of these candidate workflows was validated by the three trial pairs.
+
+## Complete finished development records
+
+[The duct archive](logs/duct/) contains 18 completed captures, 90 files, and 291,226 bytes from the coordinator's intermediate skill-development exports.
+Every existing metadata file, stdout/stderr stream, and resource-sample file is preserved byte-for-byte, including failed attempts and historical paths.
+Seventeen captures match export plan/report 02; the later completed stage-03 provenance audit is absent from that plan and is separately marked in the [manifest](logs/manifest.json), with direct central-source/intermediate hash verification.
+Each file records its central source, intermediate export, final relative path, SHA-256, and size.
+
+Two captures have nonzero exit status; failed subcommands can also appear inside successful captures.
+There are no missing stdout/stderr files, eight empty stdout/stderr streams, and one empty resource-sample file.
+No stdin was captured or invented.
+Local duct resource samples measure monitored local processes, not remote model compute.
+Agent-native histories, command captures, and DataLad records establish different evidence.
+
+The current outer native documentation invocation is still running and is **not** included as a completed capture.
+The coordinator will export it after this worker stops in a separate curation commit and verify uploaded code/checkpoint references.
+Later log packaging, replay, or publication checks do not repair historical worker outcomes or count as worker-produced quality.
+Private native transcripts, user configuration, credentials, raw retrieval trees, and private Workshop memory are outside this delivery.

+
+These are descriptive response-time results, with differential missingness and run/task composition limiting interpretation.
+They do not establish causal practice, fatigue, learning, or loss-aversion effects.

+Identical 15-case probes found `N/A` and ` n/A ` labeled `invalid_numeric_rt` instead of `missing_rt`, contrary to the frozen case-insensitive requirement; baseline passed the probes.

+[The duct archive](logs/duct/) contains 18 completed captures, 90 files, and 291,226 bytes from the coordinator's intermediate skill-development exports.
